scheme_name: ICRISAT Innovation Lab for Dryland Crops
overview: The ICRISAT Innovation Lab for Dryland Crops is part of ICRISAT's broader mission to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in agriculture for sustainable development. It supports agri-startups through training programs, incubation services, and access to funding opportunities, particularly via the Agribusiness and Innovation Platform (AIP). The lab focuses on dryland crops and provides resources for technology transfer, business development, and market linkages.
objectives: Foster innovation and entrepreneurship in agriculture for sustainable development
Support agribusiness innovation and startup development through incubation models
Provide training in business planning, financial literacy, and enterprise management
Strengthen linkages with financial institutions, technical experts, and government departments
Promote inclusive growth by empowering women and youth in agri-food enterprises
Facilitate technology transfer and commercialization of agricultural innovations
Build capacity for sustainable agricultural systems and value chain development
Create networks for cross-border collaboration in sustainable agriculture
eligibility: Participants must be government officials, field-level functionaries in agriculture, women and child welfare, rural health ministries, agri-business, or related sectors from countries in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. They should have a university degree in science, agriculture, horticulture, food processing, business management, economics, or social studies, and 2 to 3 years of relevant work experience.
benefits: Participants gain practical knowledge in food processing, packaging, marketing, and quality standards; develop business planning and financial literacy skills; strengthen linkages with key departments, technical experts, and financial institutions; improve livelihoods and household incomes; and are empowered as change agents for sustainable rural development through enterprise management training and exposure to food processing facilities and agri-business incubators.
financial_support: The program facilitates access to funding opportunities for agribusiness startups through public-private partnerships and explores financing options including government schemes. It includes a role-play exercise for pitching to investors and provides guidance on commercialization pathways, licensing, partnerships, and spin-offs.
application_process: 1. Create a login to apply for the course and furnish all requisite information. 2. Submit the application online and download the submitted application form. 3. Take a printout of the submitted application form and get appropriate signatures at all signature placeholders including English proficiency certificate, medical report, candidate undertaking form, and employer nomination form. 4. Scan the complete application document and submit physical copies to the Indian High Commission in your country. 5. Email the scanned copy of the executed application form to icrisat-ipfc@icrisat.org with copy to vishwambhar.duche@icrisat.org and babu.potta@icrisat.org.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round for various training programs, with specific deadlines varying per course (e.g., 12 January 2026 for Agri-Entrepreneurship Training for Women and Youth).
implementing_agency: International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT)
contact_details: Email: icrisat.aip@icrisat.org | Phone: +91 8455683071 (HQ, Hyderabad) | Email for research services: icrisat-research@icrisat.org
caveats: The fully sponsored training programs are exclusive to non-Indian international participants only.
Applicants may need to submit a hard copy of the filled application to the Indian Embassy/consulate in their country for funding approval.
Very limited seats are available, and eligible applications are shortlisted on a First Come First Serve basis by the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India.
